stimulus:
I met a traveller from an antique land,
Who said—"Two vast and trunkless legs of stone
Stand in the desert. . . . Near them, on the sand,
Half sunk a shattered visage lies, whose frown,
And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command,
Tell that its sculptor well those passions read
Which yet survive, stamped on these lifeless things,
The hand that mocked them, and the heart that fed;
And on the pedestal, these words appear:
My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings;
Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal Wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away."

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Trunkless legs: chromatin scars after AP-1 loss
ideas.description: Transiently induce AP-1 (e.g., FOS/JUN pulse or stimulus), then remove it by degron-mediated degradation or dominant-negative A-FOS, and at time points of days to weeks profile ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and CUT&RUN for residual open enhancers. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motif sites after the factor is gone, as with the legs that remain after the king, would indicate a memory imprint, and the question is whether it needs continued AP-1 binding.

ideas.title: Inscription vs. sand: reversibility and decay kinetics
ideas.description: Track AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN), accessibility and target transcription at repeated time points after the stimulus ends, and fit decay half-lives. Compare them with the cell division number, using synchronized or arrested cells to separate passive dilution from active maintenance, to test whether the memory is stable or erodes like the sand-covered statue.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation (primed response) assay
ideas.description: Give naive cells and previously stimulated cells (for example, fibroblasts or macrophages after injury or inflammatory exposure) a second stimulus after a rest period, and measure the faster or stronger transcriptional response by RNA-seq or nascent-RNA (PRO-seq). Compare the effect of AP-1 perturbation (CRISPRi on FOS/JUN, or loss of specific enhancers) during the first versus the second exposure to see whether AP-1 is needed to write the memory, to read it, or both.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-linked memory tracing
ideas.description: Use live reporters of AP-1 activity (FOS promoter or AP-1 response element reporters) with barcoded lineage tracing, and record each cell's history of AP-1 activity, then ask whether sister cells inherit similar states and similar future responsiveness. Co-measure single-cell multiome (RNA and ATAC) to show that AP-1 history predicts the chromatin state better than the current signal does, like a sculptor's reading of a passion that persists in a lifeless thing.

ideas.title: Synthetic imprinting by targeted AP-1 recruitment
ideas.description: Use dCas9 or a synthetic AP-1 (a tethered or optogenetic JUN/FOS) to bring AP-1 to a chosen locus for a limited time, and then test whether the locus keeps its accessibility and expression after the tool is removed. Compare wild-type motifs with motif mutants and with pioneer or SWI/SNF (BAF) recruitment-deficient variants, to show sufficiency and the mechanism of AP-1-dependent memory.
